title: Velocity at A
description: Essential: The final answer for v_A must be 2 m/s, derived from the condition that the normal force at A is zero (centripetal force equals weight).

title: Distance to B
description: Essential: The final answer for the distance x must be 5 m, found by applying the work-energy theorem from the release point to point A.

title: Minimum Speed in Air
description: Essential: The final answer for the minimum speed after leaving A must be approximately 1.94 m/s, obtained by minimizing the speed function v(t).

title: Work-Energy Setup
description: Important: The work-energy equation must correctly account for work done by the electric field, friction, and gravity between the release point and A.

title: Force Analysis at A
description: Important: The condition of zero normal force at the top of the semicircle must be used to relate centripetal acceleration to gravity.

title: Kinematics Post-A
description: Important: The horizontal and vertical velocity components after leaving A must be expressed as functions of time, incorporating the electric force and gravity.

title: Speed Minimization
description: Optional: The process of finding the time at which speed is minimum by differentiating v^2(t) or using vector principles should be shown or implied.

title: Sign of Electric Force
description: Pitfall: Incorrect sign for the work done by the electric field on the negative charge, or wrong direction of the horizontal acceleration after point A.

title: Friction Direction
description: Pitfall: Forgetting that friction on the horizontal track opposes motion, doing negative work, or misplacing it in the energy equation.
